intended: In cases one and three the shorter cycle time was recorded before the coolant was switched: 29 March precedes 4 May, and 30 September precedes 5 October. Half the evidence therefore describes runs that had already sped up when the treatment was introduced, so it cannot be evidence for the treatment. The two remaining cases are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four runs have outcome dates before the switch date: run One 'switched 4 May' but 'ran 6 minutes shorter by 29 March', and run Three 'switched 5 October' but shorter 'by 30 September' - the effect is recorded before the coolant was in use. The stated control also misses the units: 'Every shop ran its machines on the insert grade used the quarter before' yet 'every logged run was cut on a machine hired from outside', so the insert-grade control never covered the machines actually measured.

reported: Two of the four runs are measured before the coolant was ever switched in: case One 'switched 4 May' but 'ran 6 minutes shorter by 29 March', and case Three 'switched 5 October' but 'ran 7 minutes shorter by 30 September'. Those improvements predate the intervention, so half the cases cannot be evidence for it.

intended: The mid-passage line states that timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and that about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none. The minute figures are therefore tallied over roughly five sixths of the runs dispatched, while the claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, the non-reporting sixth included. Runs that come back without a finish time are not a random slice of the dispatch book, since late returns and rounds that were never closed out are exactly the runs most likely to have run long, so the 8, 5, 9 and 6 minute reductions recorded on the reporting subset are consistent with no reduction across all runs dispatched. Every case is vans out of Kettleby Wharf in February under dispatcher Verhoeven, so one reporting gap sits under all four groups at once.
reported: The timings are drawn from a narrower set than the runs the claim is about: 'Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none.' Runs with no finish time are exactly the ones most likely to have run long, so the 5-9 minute improvement is computed on a self-selected fast subset.

reported: The timing average is computed on a self-selected subset: 'Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none.' Roughly 17 percent of runs are dropped, and runs that fail to log a finish are plausibly the delayed ones, which is enough to produce the 5-9 minute improvement on its own.

intended: All four plots sit on one reserve, with one species in one spring under one warden, so the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: prey abundance on the surrounding farmland doubled from the previous year, which is an alternative cause of higher fledgling counts. The scope clause beside that fact puts every box at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range, so the food surge reaches every brood that was counted. Each plot is measured against the same reserve a year earlier rather than against an unboxed wood in the same spring, so nothing in the evidence separates the boxes from the prey peak. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the tally covering the whole set of installed boxes, so they add no second defect.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every plot: 'Prey abundance on the surrounding farmland doubled from the previous year, and every box stood at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range.' Since the comparison is to the previous spring, doubled food supply within foraging range can fully account for the 9-16 extra fledglings without the boxes contributing anything.

intended: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils enrolled for the whole term", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who left; pupils who leave part-way carry the heaviest absence, and dropping them from the denominator lowers the recorded rate on its own. All four cases are Year 9 at Brackhill Academy in one autumn term, so the same exclusion applies identically in every case and no case corrects another. The 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all.
reported: The absence figures are restricted to survivors: they 'cover the pupils enrolled for the whole term, and about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through.' The ~20 percent of pupils who left - precisely the group most likely to have poor attendance - are dropped from the post-change figures, so the 4-7 percent fall in absence can be produced by the exclusion rather than by the timetable.

reported: 'Absence figures cover the pupils enrolled for the whole term, and about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through' means a fifth of each cohort is dropped from the figures, and part-way leavers are the pupils with the worst attendance; excluding them alone lowers measured absence by more than the 4-7 percent reported.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the percentages over the scheduled runs that returned a reading, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of scheduled runs at each stack returned no reading. The claim is about the upgrade lowering particulate at the stack across its monitored period, so the population is every scheduled run and the log covers three quarters of them. Runs go missing when the analyser faults or the sample line blocks, and those conditions are not independent of what the stack was putting out, so the dropped quarter cannot be treated as a random slice of the period. All four kilns sit at Kestrel in Q1 and each carries the same quarter of missing runs, so no case in the log covers the runs the others dropped.
reported: The particulate figures 'cover the scheduled runs that returned a reading' while 'a quarter of scheduled runs at each stack returned no reading', so a quarter of runs are silently dropped and the measured population is narrower than the claim. The throughput halving is neutralised by the fixed duty cycle, but the missing quarter is not.

(The throughput halving is defused by the "fixed duty cycle" clause; the missing readings are not defused by anything.)
